dispatch.head: The Ligers put 802.5 on 720 and turn first place into a three-way tie
dispatch.dek: Chuba Hubbard, a $5 running back, scored 156. Amon-Ra St. Brown added 123.5, Jayden Daniels 116.25, Josh Allen 111.5. Jahmyr Gibbs scored 225.75 for 720 and it didn't matter; the Ligers won by 166.25 with 77 points on their bench. 720, Trash and the Ligers are all 7-3. 720 keeps the top spot on points, which is what you're left with after a week like this.

dispatch.head: Trash scores 951.5, the most by anyone this season
dispatch.dek: Christian McCaffrey 257.75, Brock Purdy 198.75, Dak Prescott 185.25, James Cook 128.5. Trash beat Wad of Hell by 339.75, the biggest margin of the week, and broke the season high, their own 881.25 from Week 2, by 70.25. They still left Cooper Kupp's 50.5 on the bench to start Tre Tucker, who scored 6.75. Some habits survive anything.

dispatch.head: Bloodfeast makes six moves in five days and posts the week's low
dispatch.dek: Ashton Dulin was added Thursday and cut Friday. Deion Burks was added at 12:41 Sunday, started, and scored 0.00. Keaton Mitchell started and scored 2. Bloodfeast scored 408.25, the lowest of the week, and its perfect lineup, 429.5, still loses to the Wet Bandits by 228.25. That's the $50 low-score penalty, paid by a team with $4 of FAAB left.

dispatch.head: Prestige benches a win and starts a man it found in BMB's trash
dispatch.dek: Reggie Virgil was added by BMB at 9:00 Thursday and cut at 9:05. Prestige picked him up at 2:44, cut Brandon Aiyuk to do it, and started him Sunday. He scored 0.00. Alvin Kamara (59.5), Josh Downs (64.75) and Jordyn Tyson (60) sat. The optimal lineup, 797.75, beats the Diamond Dogs by 30.75. Prestige lost by 118.5. The two-game winning streak is over.

dispatch.head: Nuts spend their entire FAAB on Carson Beck. He scores 7.5
dispatch.dek: Wednesday night Nuts bid $721 on Carson Beck. Sunday they started him. He scored 7.50, which works out to $96.13 a point. D.J. Moore scored 94.5 on the bench. Jordan Addison started and didn't play, Omar Cooper Jr. started and scored 0.00. Nine straight losses, 1-9, $0 of FAAB, and the Ligers are next.

dispatch.head: The Wet Bandits start Emmett Johnson. He scores 153
dispatch.dek: For two straight weeks this publication told the Wet Bandits to start Emmett Johnson. Last week we said we'd stopped asking. This week they started him, and he scored 153, the second-most of anyone on their roster. Patrick Mahomes added 194.5. The Wet Bandits scored 657.75 with a perfect lineup, beat Bloodfeast by 249.5 and are 6-4. You're welcome.

takes.0001: Six free-agent moves in five days. Ashton Dulin came in Thursday and left Friday so Rashid Shaheed could score 6. Drew Lock replaced Joe Milton, the $36 waiver claim from two weeks ago, and scored 90, the one move that worked. Deion Burks came in at 12:41 Sunday for Quentin Johnston, started, and scored 0.00. Keaton Mitchell started for 2. Kaleb Johnson sat for 21. Isaiah Likely (120.25) and J.J. McCarthy (100.25) were the only reasons this wasn't worse. 408.25, the week's low, the perfect lineup still loses by 228.25, and that's $50 to the penalty pool. 3-7, $4 of FAAB, and Wad of Hell next as a 138-point underdog.
takes.0002: Jahmyr Gibbs scored 225.75. 720 lost by 166.25. Tony Pollard (91) and CeeDee Lamb (79) were fine, and nothing else was. Christian Watson ($13) scored 27.75 and Germie Bernard 5 while Kaelon Black scored 61.25 on the bench, the second straight week Black sat in a week he belonged in the lineup. Malachi Fields ($1) added 46.5 on the bench. The optimal lineup, 711.25, still loses to the Ligers. 7-3, tied for first, still first on points with 6,906, and still $0 of FAAB. Prestige is next and MFL has 720 by 190.1, so this should be a short week.
takes.0003: 802.5, the second-best score of the week, and the Ligers are back in a tie for first. Chuba Hubbard ($5) scored 156, St. Brown 123.5, Daniels 116.25, Allen 111.5. That's the good part. The other part: 77 points on the bench again. Seth McGowan ($1) scored 63.5 there while Aaron Jones started for 54.5. Malik Washington scored 66 on the bench while Denzel Boston started for 12. Kyle Pitts sat for 27.5 while Brock Bowers, a $20 tight end, started for 13.5. Kirk Cousins scored 87.25 on the bench for a third straight week. 7-3, and Nuts are next, the biggest spread of the week.
takes.0004: They started Emmett Johnson. He scored 153. It only took two weeks of being told. Patrick Mahomes scored 194.5, Caleb Douglas ($1) 53.25, Tee Higgins 49.5, Adonai Mitchell 44.25, and the lineup was perfect: 657.75, zero points left on the bench. Beat Bloodfeast by 249.5. The waiver money is still a question. Mack Hollins cost $51 and scored 36. Corey Kiner cost $31 and scored 12.5. Dallas Goedert was cut for them. 6-4, $230 of FAAB, and Resistance next, with the Wet Bandits favored by 69.6.
takes.0005: 951.5, the best score of the season, topping their own Week 2 high by 70.25. McCaffrey 257.75, Purdy 198.75, Prescott 185.25, Cook 128.5, Kittle 55.5. Trash beat Wad by 339.75. The only blemish is a familiar one: Tre Tucker started and scored 6.75 while Cooper Kupp, a $1 receiver, scored 50.5 on the bench. Even with that, 43.75 from perfect. Two-game skid over, 7-3, tied for first, and $750 of FAAB. The Diamond Dogs are next, MFL has Trash by 8.5, and the Dogs just played a perfect lineup.
takes.0006: Wednesday: $721 on Carson Beck, every dollar of FAAB Nuts had. Sunday: Beck started and scored 7.50. That's $96.13 per point. D.J. Moore scored 94.5 on the bench. MarShawn Lloyd, added Thursday, scored 26 on the bench. Jordan Addison started and didn't play. Omar Cooper Jr. started and scored 0.00. Keon Coleman ($16) scored 8.25. Trevor Lawrence (151.5) and Cam Skattebo (122) deserved better. 422, and the perfect lineup, 542.5, still loses by 65. Nine straight, 1-9, $0 of FAAB, and the Ligers next as a 232.7-point underdog, the biggest spread of the week.
takes.0007: Two straight wins, and it wasn't close. Jared Goff (117.25), C.J. Stroud (112.75) and Deebo Samuel ($6, 112.25) did the heavy lifting. Laquon Treadwell, picked up at 8:23 Sunday morning, started and scored 43. The bench is still a problem: Ryan Flournoy scored 78.25 there and Jahan Dotson 47.25, while Rhamondre Stevenson ($8) started and scored 2.75. 86.5 points from perfect against a team that didn't need it. 4-6, and BMB next, with the Scallywags favored by 12.7.
takes.0008: Lost by 339.75 and left 148.75 points on the bench, the most in the league. Cam Ward scored 107.25 on the bench while Jordan Love, a $23 quarterback, started for 65. Tre Harris (64.5), Antonio Williams (56.5) and Jerry Jeudy (55.5) all sat while Jalen Coker started for 1.5 and Khalil Shakir for 34. Bijan Robinson, $51, scored 65. The perfect lineup, 760.5, still loses by 191, so the bench was only a matter of pride. 6-4, and Bloodfeast is next, with MFL giving Wad 138 points.
takes.0009: Won with 561.25, the lowest winning score of the week, and left 102 points on the bench to do it. Cyrus Allen ($1) scored 58 on the bench, Ja'Kobi Lane 45.75, Dalton Kincaid 43.5. Starting instead: A.J. Brown, $35, 20.25. Kyren Williams, $18, 18.25. Mike Gesicki, 6.75, a week after Gesicki's 8.25 helped lose to Prestige. Joe Burrow (211.25) and Konata Mumpfield, a Thursday pickup, (60.75) carried. 6-4, and the Wet Bandits next, favored by 69.6.
takes.0010: Lost to the Diamond Dogs by 118.5 with a lineup that would have won by 30.75. Reggie Virgil, cut by BMB five minutes after BMB added him, was picked up Thursday at the cost of Brandon Aiyuk, started, and scored 0.00. Devaughn Vele started for 10.5, Braelon Allen for 24.5. On the bench: Josh Downs 64.75, Jordyn Tyson ($13) 60, Alvin Kamara 59.5. Then Sunday they cut Kyler Murray for Ashton Dulin, the receiver Bloodfeast didn't want, and benched him. George Pickens scored 183.75 for nothing. 2-8, two-game streak over, and 720 next as a 190.1-point underdog.
takes.0011: Lost by 45 with a lineup that would have won by 33.75. Kyle McCord, picked up Thursday for Malik Willis, scored 69.25 on the bench while Drake Maye ($19) started for 17.5. Last week this publication said start Demario Douglas after his 76.5 on the bench. They did. He scored 3. Dylan Sampson (26.25) sat while Tucker Kraft started for 14.25. Darren Waller, the reason Reggie Virgil got cut after five minutes, scored 18 on the bench. Parker Washington ($17) scored 164, the week's best wasted effort. Two straight losses, 5-5, and the Scallywags next.
takes.0012: 767 with a perfect lineup, not a point left on the bench, and four straight wins. Ja'Marr Chase scored 198.25, Jaxon Smith-Njigba ($14) 178.25, Breece Hall 70.75, Harold Fannin 68.25. Tank Dell cost $350 on waivers Wednesday, with Chris Godwin cut to make room, and scored 15.75, which was still the right call, which says something about the alternatives. 6-4, and Trash next in the closest spread of the week, 8.5 points.

Team of the Week.text: 951.5, the season high, beating their own Week 2 mark by 70.25. McCaffrey 257.75, Purdy 198.75, Prescott 185.25. Beat Wad by 339.75.

Biggest Bust.text: 408.25, the week's low. Six moves in five days, a Sunday pickup started for 0.00, and the perfect lineup still loses by 228.25. $50 to the penalty pool.

Luckiest Win.text: Won with 561.25, the lowest winning score of the week, while benching 102 points. BMB's optimal lineup would have won.

threads: Standings after Wk 10: E720, FBT and Ligers 7-3 (E720 first on PF, 6,906); Wet Bandits, Wad, DD and Viva 6-4; BMB 5-5; Scally 4-6; Bloodfeast 3-7; Prestige 2-8; Nuts 1-9.
Streaks: DD W4, Scally W2; Ligers, FBT, Wet Bandits, Viva W1; Nuts L9, BMB L2; E720, Wad, Prestige (W2 snapped), Bloodfeast L1.

Wk 10 high: FBT 951.5 (season high; previous FBT 881.25 Wk 2). Low: Bloodfeast 408.25 (penalty pool). Biggest margin: FBT +339.75 over Wad. Closest: Viva over BMB by 45. Perfect lineups: Wet Bandits 657.75, DD 767.
Nuts: $721 waiver on Carson Beck Wed (all FAAB, now $0), started him, 7.50. D.J. Moore 94.5 on bench. Addison started DNP, Omar Cooper Jr. 0.00. L9.
Wet Bandits finally started Emmett Johnson (153) after the Wk 9 and Wk 10 previews. Waivers: Mack Hollins $51 (36), Corey Kiner $31 (12.5), cut Goedert. FAAB $230.

Bloodfeast: six FA moves Thu-Sun. Dulin added Thu, cut Fri for Shaheed (6). Drew Lock for Joe Milton (90). Deion Burks added Sun 12:41 for Quentin Johnston, started, 0.00. Keaton Mitchell started 2. FAAB $4.
Reggie Virgil: BMB added Thu 9:00, cut 9:05 for Darren Waller. Prestige added Thu 2:44 (cut Aiyuk), started him, 0.00. Prestige also cut Kyler Murray Sun for Ashton Dulin (benched).
Prestige optimal 797.75 would have beaten DD 767. BMB optimal 595 would have beaten Viva 561.25. Viva left 102 on bench (Cyrus Allen 58, Lane, Kincaid), started Gesicki 6.75 again.
Ligers: Hubbard ($5) 156. Bench again: McGowan 63.5, Malik Washington 66, Pitts 27.5; Cousins 87.25 on bench third straight week. E720: Kaelon Black benched again (61.25), Gibbs 225.75 in a loss.
DD: Tank Dell $350 waiver (cut Godwin), 15.75. FBT: Kupp ($1) 50.5 benched for Tre Tucker 6.75 again. Wad benched 148.75 incl. Cam Ward 107.25 over Love.

0004-0002.head: Game of the Week: the new leader hosts the week's high scorer
0004-0002.text: 720 (6-2) just beat Trash by 288 with a perfect lineup and leads the league with 5,469 points. The Wet Bandits (5-3) just scored 793, the best of the week. MFL has 720 by 15.8, the closest spread of the week. The Wet Bandits lead the series 10-6, but 720 has won the last two, 822.25–510.75 last year and 817.75–683.25 in Week 3. Gibbs, Pollard and Geno Smith against Tee Higgins, Patrick Mahomes and Michael Wilson. The Wet Bandits' tiebreaker: start Emmett Johnson this time.

0001-0003.head: Bloodfeast faces its own quarterback
0001-0003.text: Bloodfeast (2-6) sold Jayden Daniels and Stefon Diggs to the Ligers (6-2) on Wednesday. Now it plays them. MFL has the Ligers by 205.5, the biggest spread of the week. Bloodfeast leads the series 19-15, but the Ligers won the last two, 773–491.25 last year and 608–442.5 in Week 3. The Ligers' biggest threat is their own lineup decisions: Josh Allen, Daniels or Kirk Cousins, who scored 148.25 on the bench last week. Bloodfeast has Daniel Jones.

0012-0011.head: The hottest team in the league against the most frustrating one
0012-0011.text: BMB (5-3) has won five straight. The Diamond Dogs (4-4) have won two straight while benching 479.25 points over those two weeks. MFL has BMB by 44.4. BMB leads the series 14-12, but the Diamond Dogs won Week 3 679–413. Bhayshul Tuten, Drake Maye and Demario Douglas against Ja'Marr Chase, Harold Fannin and Jaxon Smith-Njigba. If the Diamond Dogs ever start Bo Nix, this could get ugly.

0005-0007.head: Trash needs a bounce-back, and the Scallywags are right there
0005-0007.text: Trash (6-2) lost by 288 with a perfect lineup. The Scallywags (2-6) benched Tyler Allgeier's 181.5. MFL has Trash by 153.3. The series is 2-2, and Trash won Week 3 786.5–610.25. Dak Prescott, James Cook and Josh Jacobs should be enough, as long as Tre Tucker remembers how to score. For the Scallywags: start Allgeier.

0009-0010.head: Prestige is favored. Really.
0009-0010.text: Prestige (1-7) just won its first game. Resistance (5-3) just got 240.5 from Joe Burrow. MFL has Prestige by 81.7 anyway. Resistance leads the series 17-15 and won Week 3 637.75–507, but Prestige took last year's game 569–461. Braelon Allen and Kyler Murray against Burrow, Jaylen Warren and Mike Gesicki. If Prestige wins two straight, it's no longer a fluke. It's a trend.

0006-0008.head: Nuts try to stop the bleeding
0006-0008.text: Nuts (1-7) have lost seven straight, scored 327 and traded away Tony Pollard. Wad of Hell (5-3) benched Cam Ward's 138.5 last week. MFL has Wad by 123.8. Nuts lead the series 15-12, but Wad has won the last four, including 785.75–577.5 in Week 3. Jordan Love, Trey McBride and Bijan Robinson against Trevor Lawrence, Ashton Jeanty and Jaylen Waddle. Nuts: start D.J. Moore.

0003-0002.head: Game of the Week: the leader hosts the team that fell out of first
0003-0002.text: 720 (7-2) just scored 800.75, the best of the week, and sits alone in first. The Ligers (6-3) have lost two straight, the second to the team that sold them their quarterback. MFL has 720 by 52.1. The Ligers lead the series 20-9 and won both meetings last year, 877.25–630.5 and 670.5–511.75. CeeDee Lamb, Christian Watson and a $2 Shedeur Sanders against Josh Allen, Jayden Daniels and Brock Bowers. The Ligers' biggest opponent remains the Ligers' lineup.

0005-0008.head: Two 6-3 teams, one going the wrong way
0005-0008.text: Trash (6-3) has lost two straight and started a player who didn't play. Wad of Hell (6-3) just won by 389.75. MFL has Trash by 96.5 anyway. Wad leads the series 16-13. Last year they split three games: Wad 551.75–423.25, Trash 889.5–525.5, Wad 782.25–689. Brock Purdy, Dak Prescott and James Cook against Jordan Love, Bijan Robinson and Javonte Williams. Trash: check the injury report this time.

0011-0009.head: The closest spread of the week
0011-0009.text: BMB (5-4) just saw its five-game streak end. Resistance (5-4) just lost to Prestige by benching a $1 running back's 72.75. MFL has BMB by 9.1. Resistance leads the series 18-13 and won both meetings last year, 626.5–512 and 682–653.5. Drake Maye and Luther Burden against Joe Burrow and Justice Hill, assuming Resistance has learned where Hill goes. BMB: Demario Douglas scored 76.5 on your bench. Start him.

0001-0004.head: Bloodfeast tries for two straight
0001-0004.text: Bloodfeast (3-6) just beat the Ligers with a $36 waiver quarterback. The Wet Bandits (5-4) just lost to 720 with Emmett Johnson on the bench again. MFL has the Wet Bandits by 20.9. Bloodfeast leads the series 11-4 and won 755–576 in 2024 and both meetings last year, the second 624.5–610. Puka Nacua against Kenneth Walker III and Patrick Mahomes. Wet Bandits: we've stopped asking about Emmett Johnson.

0012-0010.head: Prestige goes for three
0012-0010.text: Prestige (2-7) has won two straight. The Diamond Dogs (5-4) have won three straight and finally started Bo Nix. MFL has the Diamond Dogs by 51.6. Prestige leads the series 16-14 and won both meetings last year, 850.5–635.25 and 727.25–709.75. Ja'Marr Chase and Bo Nix against Michael Penix Jr. and Matthew Stafford. If the Diamond Dogs bench 145 points again, this one gets interesting.

0007-0006.head: Nuts host the one team that might let them win
0007-0006.text: Nuts (1-8) have lost eight straight and just scored 277.75. The Scallywags (3-6) just got 221 from C.J. Stroud. MFL has the Scallywags by 92.7. The Scallywags lead the series 2-1, but Nuts won last year's second meeting 513.25–419.25, which is the most encouraging thing anyone can say about Nuts right now. Trevor Lawrence and Ashton Jeanty against Stroud, Matthew Golden and Bucky Irving. Nuts: maybe not Emanuel Wilson.

0008-0001.head: Wad of Hell visits the week's lowest scorer
0008-0001.text: Bloodfeast (3-7) just scored 408.25 and paid the penalty pool. Wad of Hell (6-4) just lost by 339.75 with 148.75 points on the bench. MFL has Wad by 138. Bloodfeast leads the series 17-7 and won the last meeting 784.75–473.75 last year, after Wad won the first 462–337.75. Bijan Robinson, Drake London and Nico Collins against Isaiah Likely, J.J. McCarthy and whoever Bloodfeast picks up Sunday at 12:41. Wad: Cam Ward goes in the lineup.

0010-0002.head: 720 gets the softest landing in the league
0010-0002.text: 720 (7-3) just lost first place outright to the Ligers. Prestige (2-8) just benched a win. MFL has 720 by 190.1. 720 leads the series 10-9 and has won the last three, including 804–663.75 last year. Jahmyr Gibbs and CeeDee Lamb against George Pickens and Omarion Hampton. Prestige: start Kamara, Downs and Tyson, then see what happens.

0006-0003.head: The biggest spread of the week
0006-0003.text: Nuts (1-9) have lost nine straight and just spent $721 on a 7.5-point quarterback. The Ligers (7-3) just scored 802.5. MFL has the Ligers by 232.7. The Ligers lead the series 12-10, but Nuts won last year's meeting 698.25–636.25, which Nuts fans are allowed to bring up. Josh Allen, Jayden Daniels and Chuba Hubbard against Trevor Lawrence and Cam Skattebo. The Ligers' only threat is their own bench, which scored 77 more than their lineup needed last week.

0009-0004.head: The Wet Bandits have found their running back
0009-0004.text: The Wet Bandits (6-4) just started Emmett Johnson and got 153. Resistance (6-4) just won with the lowest winning score of the week. MFL has the Wet Bandits by 69.6. The Wet Bandits lead the series 9-2 and have won the last three, the most recent 474–450.75 last year. Mahomes and Johnson against Joe Burrow and Derrick Henry. Resistance: Mike Gesicki is not a starter.

0012-0005.head: Game of the Week: the season high against the hottest team
0012-0005.text: Trash (7-3) just scored 951.5, the most by anyone this season. The Diamond Dogs (6-4) have won four straight and just played a perfect lineup. MFL has Trash by 8.5, the closest spread of the week. Trash leads the series 10-9, but the Diamond Dogs won last year's meeting 706.75–680.5. McCaffrey, Purdy and Prescott against Ja'Marr Chase and Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Trash: Cooper Kupp over Tre Tucker. It's not complicated.

0007-0011.head: The Scallywags are favored. Read that again.
0007-0011.text: The Scallywags (4-6) have won two straight. BMB (5-5) has lost two straight, the last one with a winning lineup on its bench. MFL has the Scallywags by 12.7. BMB has won both meetings, 742.25–637 in 2024 and 757.25–500.5 last year. Goff, Stroud and Deebo Samuel against Parker Washington and Drake Maye, or Kyle McCord, if BMB learned anything.
